clue.text: In spring weather that's bad, run game

parts.note: to spring is to leap

indicators.note: run is placed in the middle of the spring-plus-bad-weather string

parts.note: fog is weather nobody wants
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: Somebody heads out in miserable spring weather for a jog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' at the very start is the container signal, though it reads like an ordinary preposition about the season.
explanation.definitionFit: Leapfrog is a children's playground game of vaulting over a bent back.

clue.text: See my girl injured here — Louisa?

definitions.text: See my girl injured here — Louisa?

indicators.note: hurt, so the letters are knocked out of shape

explanation.surface: Someone points to where a young woman named Louisa was hurt.
explanation.walkthrough: In Jane Austen's Persuasion, Louisa Musgrove is injured jumping from the Cobb at Lyme Regis, a Dorset seaside town.
explanation.definitionFit: This Dorset resort is the scene of Louisa Musgrove's fall in Persuasion, so the whole clue points to the town.

clue.text: A line's a sound one to prosecute

indicators.note: the phrase is spoken, and what is heard is the answer

parts.note: an actor's line is a cue, so this reads a cue's a

explanation.surface: An actor's line sounds like a charge being brought.
explanation.definitionFit: An accuser brings charges, one who prosecutes or alleges wrongdoing.

clue.text: Like cat to curl round tip of tail in snow

indicators.note: the cat-like word wraps itself about the letter, as a cat curls up

parts.note: furry describes a cat's coat

indicators.note: only the first letter of the following word is used

explanation.surface: A cat curls its tail round itself in the snow.
explanation.definitionFit: A flurry is a brief light fall of snow, so snow here is shorthand for it.

clue.text: From this, be let out? I would be free

definitions.text: From this, be let out? I would be free

indicators.note: the letters are set loose into a new order

explanation.surface: A prisoner in a dungeon wishes for release.
explanation.walkthrough: An oubliette is a dungeon reached only through a trapdoor in the roof, from which escape is hopeless.
explanation.definitionFit: A dungeon from which nobody escapes is the place a prisoner would long to leave.

clue.text: Author having tea tucked into cake

indicators.note: one piece is folded inside the other, like a napkin tucked in

parts.note: a bun is a small cake
cha (char) is British slang for tea

explanation.surface: A writer enjoys a cuppa with a teacake.
explanation.definitionFit: John Buchan was a Scottish novelist, writer of The Thirty-Nine Steps.

clue.text: Deficit in prosperous time — none the less, there's attractive growth

indicators.note: the deficit word goes into the boom word
one O, a nought or none, is removed

parts.note: a boom is a period of prosperity
a loss is a deficit

explanation.surface: Despite a shortfall during good times, there is pleasing development.
explanation.walkthrough: 'none the less' removes one O from BOOM, leaving BOM, into which LOSS goes.
explanation.definitionFit: Blossom is the flowering of a plant, a pretty kind of growth.

clue.text: Exciting of weather to keep cold

indicators.note: the weather word holds on to the extra letter

parts.note: climatic means relating to climate or weather

explanation.surface: Thrilling weather that holds on to a chill.
explanation.definitionFit: A climactic moment is the thrilling peak of a story.

clue.text: Bible found in seaweed in coastal province

indicators.note: the Bible is located inside the seaweed

parts.note: algae include seaweeds
RV is the Revised Version of the Bible

explanation.surface: Scripture turns up among the seaweed on a beach.
explanation.definitionFit: The Algarve is the southern coastal region of Portugal.

clue.text: Compere holds a coat

indicators.note: one piece grips the other within it

parts.note: MC, master of ceremonies, is a compere

explanation.surface: A host on stage keeps hold of someone's coat.
explanation.definitionFit: Mac is short for mackintosh, a waterproof raincoat.

clue.text: Inappropriate, failing to develop?

definitions.meaning: read whimsically as not becoming anything, never turning into something

explanation.definitionFit: Unseemly behaviour is unsuitable; the second sense splits the word as not-becoming.

clue.text: Keep back — others fall

parts.note: the rest means the others
rain is what falls from clouds

explanation.surface: Hold back while everyone else tumbles.
explanation.definitionFit: To restrain someone is to hold them in check, synonym for keeping back.

clue.text: Like the night, perhaps southern, to linger

parts.note: to tarry is to linger

explanation.surface: A southern evening that makes one want to stay out late.
explanation.definitionFit: A night full of visible stars is described as starlit; 'perhaps' marks the night as one example.

clue.text: Black scrap turned into dress

indicators.note: the joined pieces are read backwards, turned round to form the answer

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils
a rag is a scrap of cloth

explanation.surface: A dark remnant of fabric gets made into a frock.
explanation.definitionFit: Garb means clothing or attire, synonym for dress as a noun.

clue.text: Refuses to touch cannabis which terrified Billy Bones

parts.note: unions black goods, refusing to handle them
pot is slang for cannabis

explanation.surface: A man will not go near drugs that frightened an old pirate.
explanation.walkthrough: In Treasure Island the pirate Billy Bones dies of fright on receiving the black spot, a pirates' death warning.
explanation.definitionFit: The black spot is the pirates' summons in Treasure Island that terrifies Billy Bones.

clue.text: One proverbially cruel to kill dog, say, turned in

indicators.note: the reversed pet is placed inside the word for killing

parts.note: to smother is to kill by suffocation

indicators.note: the pet is flipped round end to end

parts.note: a dog is one example of a pet

explanation.surface: A heartless relative sets out to do away with the family dog.
explanation.walkthrough: The wicked stepmother of Cinderella and Snow White is the proverbial cruel figure; 'turned' gives TEP.
explanation.definitionFit: The wicked stepmother of fairy tales is the proverbial figure of cruelty.

clue.text: Theatre put up with old artist

indicators.note: in a down clue the word is raised, read from the bottom

parts.note: rep is repertory theatre
former means old, earlier

explanation.surface: A theatre accommodates a once-famous painter.
explanation.definitionFit: A performer is an artist in the sense of an entertainer.

clue.text: Rogue outlaw holds up passenger

indicators.note: in a down clue the outlaw sits underneath, supporting the passenger

parts.note: a rider is a passenger
a hood is a gangster or outlaw

explanation.surface: A bandit stages a hold-up of a traveller.
explanation.walkthrough: Rogue Riderhood is a villainous boatman in Dickens's Our Mutual Friend, so 'Rogue' is his first name.
explanation.definitionFit: Rogue is the given name of this Dickens character, so the first name leads to the surname.

clue.text: For duke, leaves Hill building Gothic

definitions.meaning: the leaves on a duke's coronet are of this fruit plant
Horace Walpole's Twickenham villa gave its name to a Gothic Revival style

explanation.definitionFit: Strawberry leaves adorn a ducal coronet, and Strawberry Hill Gothic is an eighteenth-century architectural style.

clue.text: Using foot tread without notice across line in pub

indicators.note: the shortened word stretches over the line, enclosing it
without here means lacking, so the tread word goes on minus its notice

parts.note: taken as written
an ad is a notice
the oche is the throwing line in a game of darts

explanation.surface: Someone steps carefully across a pub floor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Using' is a link. The oche is the throwing line in darts, a game played in British pubs; 'without' leaves TRE, and 'across' wraps it round the oche.
explanation.definitionFit: A trochee is a metrical foot of one stressed then one unstressed syllable.

clue.text: Mushroom: almost approve eating it if under weight

indicators.note: the shortened word takes the other letters inside
the final letter is dropped

parts.note: to bless is to approve

indicators.note: in a down clue the second piece goes below the first

explanation.surface: A diner almost blesses a meal if it weighs little.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' leaves BLES; 'if under' stacks W above IT in this down clue, and 'eating' puts that pair inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Blewits are edible woodland mushrooms with lilac-tinted stems.

clue.text: Lectured husband, taken in for questioning?

indicators.note: the husband is brought inside, as a suspect is

parts.note: the CID, the Criminal Investigation Department, is the police branch that questions suspects

explanation.surface: A spouse is told off after being hauled to the station.
explanation.definitionFit: Chid is an old past tense of chide, to scold or rebuke.

clue.text: He painted pictures of pig and horse

parts.note: a hog is a pig
art is pictures
H is slang for heroin, known as horse

explanation.surface: An artist depicts farm animals.
explanation.definitionFit: William Hogarth was an eighteenth-century English painter and engraver.

clue.text: Big venues have way to lift opera

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for street, a way

indicators.note: in a down clue the opera is raised, read bottom to top

parts.note: Aida is Verdi's opera

explanation.surface: Large arenas find a way to stage a grand opera.
explanation.definitionFit: Stadia is a plural of stadium, large sports venues.

clue.text: Something for coffee break that sits on computer

definitions.meaning: a biscuit, in American usage, eaten with a coffee
a small data file a website stores on your machine

explanation.definitionFit: A biscuit is called this in the US, and websites leave small tracking files of the same name.

clue.text: Tenant perhaps puts too much in locker

indicators.note: the excess is put inside the other word

parts.note: a cager is one who locks something in a cage
OTT, over the top, means too much

explanation.surface: A renter crams far too much into a storage cupboard.
explanation.definitionFit: A cottager lives in a cottage, often renting it, so is a tenant by example.

clue.text: Wild, like a kangaroo?

definitions.meaning: read literally, jumping and bounding about in a frenzy

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means furious; a kangaroo, bounding about, might be described as literally hopping.

clue.text: First to reach home opening letter

indicators.note: the first letter of the next word is taken

parts.note: HO is an abbreviation for house, a home

explanation.surface: Whoever gets home first opens the post.
explanation.definitionFit: Rho is the seventeenth letter of the Greek alphabet.

clue.text: Demoralisation as part of organisation has no heart

parts.note: a dept, department, is part of an organisation

indicators.note: the central letter of the word is removed

explanation.surface: Morale slumps in a section of a company lacking spirit.
explanation.definitionFit: To be in the depths is to be at the lowest point of despair, so it stands for demoralisation.

clue.text: Strangely, hard debater was whispering

indicators.note: the letters are put into an unusual arrangement

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: Oddly, a tough debater spoke in a hushed voice.
explanation.definitionFit: To breathe words is to say them very softly, as a whisper.
